predecessors.name: Kingdom of Poland
predecessors.text: Pomerelia, Gdańsk Pomerania: the Duchy of Gdańsk and the Duchy of Świecie and Lubiszewo

successors.name: Teutonic Order
successors.text: Pomerelia, Gdańsk Pomerania: the Duchy of Gdańsk and the Duchy of Świecie and Lubiszewo

ledger.x: 1273: 'Brandenburg returned Gdańsk to Mestwin while he paid feudal homage to the margraves' for Sławno and Słupsk.

Summer 1308: 'a rebellion was incited by the local Swienca family' and Brandenburg intervened, occupying the duchy's west (Pomerelia page: 'the city of Gdańsk was occupied by the Margraviate of Brandenburg' in 1308).

1308: the Teutonic Order, invited by Władysław's governor Bogusza, enters the duchy; on 13 November 1308 'the order's forces ... forced their way into the town' of Gdańsk, which was captured and largely destroyed.
13 November 1308: Gdańsk falls to the Teutonic Order.
September 1309: 'Margrave Waldemar of Brandenburg-Stendal sold his claim to the territory' to the Order for 10,000 marks (Treaty of Soldin).
September 1309: the Treaty of Soldin ends the contest; the Order holds the whole duchy.

1309: 'The Order took the whole duchy after the Treaty of Soldin'; the Pomerelia page: the Teutonic Knights took the area, 'annexing and incorporating it into the Teutonic Order state in 1309'. Świecie and Tczew were conquered after Poland refused compensation for Gdańsk.
1309: the Duchy of Pomerelia is annexed into the State of the Teutonic Order; the infobox lists it as a fiefdom of Poland (1294-1308).

wars.name: Świętopełk II's wars with the Teutonic Order
wars.outcome: The Old Prussian revolt of 1242 came 'in the context of these alliances'; peace came with the Treaty of Christburg in 1249 and the Vistula-dues settlement of 1253.

wars.name: Mestwin II's war with Wartislaw and Brandenburg
wars.outcome: Mestwin expelled Wartislaw from Gdańsk with the margraves' aid in 1270/71; the margraves stayed until the 1273 treaty returned Gdańsk against homage for Sławno and Słupsk.

wars.name: Teutonic takeover of Gdańsk
wars.outcome: Brandenburg occupied the west in summer 1308; the Order took Gdańsk on 13 November 1308, then the whole duchy after the Treaty of Soldin in September 1309.

certainty.note: The pages give cities (Gdańsk, Świecie, Tczew, Sławno, Słupsk) and rivers, not boundaries; the western frontier with the Pomeranian dukes moved by dukes' agreements.
